content: In 1979, a study conducted in a hospital in Swaziland identified 65 cases of Haemophilus ducreyi (HD), 25 cases of Treponema pallidum (TP), 18 cases of lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV), 17 cases of herpes simplex virus (HSV), 5 mixed infections, and no cases without a diagnosis. In 2001, a primary health center in Ethiopia reported 2 cases of TP. A 1980 study of 100 patients from a sexually transmitted infection (STI) clinic in Kenya found 48 cases of HD, 10 cases of TP, 6 cases of HSV, 6 mixed infections, no LGV, and 36 individuals with no infections. Between 2002 and 2004, 307 individuals from an STI clinic in Taiwan, China, were studied, revealing 21 cases of TP. In 1986, 210 individuals from an STI clinic in Rwanda were examined, showing 37 cases of TP, 32 cases of HSV, 24 cases of HD, 13 cases of LGV, 29 mixed infections, and 75 individuals with no infections. From 2000 to 2001, 227 individuals from an STI clinic in China were studied, identifying 78 cases of TP, 43 cases of HSV, 28 cases of TP and HSV co-infection, 76 individuals with no diagnosis, and no cases of HD. In 1998–1999, 96 individuals from an STI clinic in China were examined, revealing 23 cases of TP, 33 cases of HSV, 40 individuals with no pathogen identified, and no cases of HD. In 2005, 76 individuals presenting at a medical center in Mozambique were studied, showing 47 cases of HSV, 3 cases of LGV, 3 cases of HD, no cases of donovanosis or TP, 23 individuals with no diagnosis, and 2 mixed infections involving HSV and LGV. In 1994, 42 women from a health center and hospital dispensary in Rwanda were studied, with 34 cases of TP identified. Similarly, 38 men from the same location in Rwanda in 1994 showed 37 cases of TP. Between 1995 and 1996, 81 men from STI clinics in the Dominican Republic were studied, revealing 5% TP, 26% HD, and 43% HSV. During the same period, 63 men from STI clinics in Peru were examined, showing 10% TP, 5% HD, and 43% HSV. In 2008–2009, 194 patients from STI clinics in India were studied, identifying 76 cases of HSV, 27 cases of TP, 17 mixed infections, and 1 case of HD. A 1990 study of 373 individuals revealed 147 cases of HD, 52 cases of TP, 7 cases of HSV, 8 cases of LGV, 1 case of donovanosis, 37 mixed infections, and 29 individuals with no diagnosis. In 2010–2011, 90 patients from an STI clinic in India were examined, showing 6 cases of TP, 66 cases of HSV, and no cases of HD, LGV, or donovanosis. In 1993–1994, 105 patients from an STI clinic in Lesotho were studied, revealing 56% HD, 23% syphilis, and 26% HSV. Between 2000 and 2001, 587 individuals from an STI clinic in South Africa were examined, showing 48% HSV, 14% TP, 11% CT-LGV, 10% HD, and 1% donovanosis. In 1995, 156 individuals from an STI clinic in Brazil were studied, revealing 31% TP. In 2015, 70 individuals from clinics in Zimbabwe were examined, showing 17 cases of HSV, 8 cases of TP, 1 case of CT-LGV, and no cases of HD. Between 1992 and 1993, 778 individuals from an STI clinic in Malawi were studied, revealing 129 cases of TP and 204 cases of HD. In 1993–1994, 100 individuals from an STI clinic in Lesotho were examined, showing 56 cases of HD, 26 cases of HSV, 23 cases of TP, and 7 cases of CT. In 1998–1999, 137 individuals from an STD clinic in Malawi were studied, revealing 47 cases of HSV, 41 cases of HD, and 5 cases of TP. Another study in Malawi, published in 2003, examined 136 individuals, showing 3% TP, 30% HD, and 35% HSV. In Jamaica, 304 individuals were studied, revealing 158 cases of HSV, 72 cases of HD, and 31 cases of TP. Between 1990 and 1992, 446 men from a sexual health clinic in the USA were studied, revealing 45 cases of TP, 118 cases of HD, and 57 cases of HSV. In Uganda, 98 patients from an urban STD clinic (date unclear, before 1995) were examined, showing 48 cases of HSV and 11 cases of TP. In Madagascar, 61 attendees of a public STD clinic with genital ulcer disease (GUD) in 1992–1993 were studied, revealing 56% syphilis, 29% LGV, 20% chancroid, and 2% HSV. In 1997, 196 attendees of an STD clinic in Madagascar with GUD were studied, revealing 61 cases of HD, 51 cases of TP, 15 cases of HSV, 3 cases of TP and HSV co-infection, 2 cases of HD and TP co-infection, and 1 case of HD and HSV co-infection. Between 1992 and 1993, 778 individuals from an STD clinic in Malawi were studied, revealing 204 cases of HD and 137 cases of TP. In 1988–1989, 100 individuals from an STI clinic in South Africa were examined, showing 40 cases of TP, 18 cases of HSV, 16 cases of CG, 14 cases of HD, 6 cases of LGV, 18 individuals with no diagnosis, and 13 cases of multiple infections. In India, 201 individuals from an STI clinic in 2008–2009 were studied, revealing 49 cases of HSV, 20 cases of TP, 3 cases of CG, 30 cases of HD, and 1 case of LGV. In 1989, 100 men from an STI clinic in South Africa were examined, showing 29 cases of TP, 12 cases of HD, 9 cases of CG, 9 cases of HSV, 3 cases of LGV, 14 mixed infections, and 24 individuals with no diagnosis. In Gambia, 104 patients from an STI clinic (before 1987) were studied, revealing 54 cases of HD, 23 cases of TP, 7 cases of LGV, 6 cases of HSV, 28 individuals with no diagnosis, and 15 mixed infections. In 1994, 516 individuals from STI clinics in the USA were studied, revealing 16 cases of HD, 51 cases of TP, 320 cases of HSV, 13 mixed infections, and 116 individuals with no diagnosis. In 2005, 53 women from an STI clinic in Brazil were examined, showing 28 cases of HSV and 1 case of TP. In 1994, 302 patients from an STI clinic in India were studied, revealing 79 cases of HSV, 69 cases of HD, 29 cases of TP, 7% multiple infections, and 104 individuals with no diagnosis. Between 2002 and 2006, 100 individuals from a community cohort in Uganda were studied, revealing 64 cases of HSV, 1 case of HD, 29 individuals with no diagnosis, 5 cases of TP, and 1 mixed infection. Between 2005 and 2006, 613 men from primary healthcare in South Africa were examined, showing 451 cases of HSV, 30 cases of TP, 10 cases of HD, and 126 individuals with no diagnosis. Between 2004 and 2006, 813 individuals from India were studied, revealing 8 cases of TP, 79 cases of HSV-2, and no cases of HD. In 1994–1995, 143 individuals from an STI clinic in the USA were examined, showing 47 cases of HD, 16 cases of TP, 39 cases of HSV, 12 mixed infections, and 29 individuals with no diagnosis. In 1996, 372 individuals from an STI clinic in Amsterdam were studied, revealing 208 cases of HSV, 12 cases of TP, and 3 cases of HD.
